title: Low-Pass Filter - Band 66 (AWS) for Public Safety Band Filter
subtitle: Design Validation and Performance Characterization
author: Dr. Ahmed Al-Farsi

sections.1_OBJECTIVE: This document describes the design, simulation, and characterization of a Low-Pass Filter filter targeting Band 66 (AWS) for Public Safety Band Filter. The filter is designed on Quartz substrate with a target center frequency of 5863.5 MHz and bandwidth of 187.4 MHz. The objective is to validate that the filter meets the required insertion loss, rejection, and linearity specifications for integration into the Public Safety Band Filter module. This design iteration addresses feedback from the previous revision regarding out-of-band rejection improvements and temperature stability.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Filter Type: Low-Pass Filter
- Frequency Band: Band 66 (AWS)
- Application: Public Safety Band Filter
- Substrate: Quartz
- Package: QFN (Quad Flat No-Lead)
- Design Tool: Matlab RF Toolbox R2024b
- Design Center: Irvine Design Center

This specification applies to all variants of the Low-Pass Filter design targeting Band 66 (AWS). Results are used to qualify the design for mass production release.
sections.3_DESIGN_PARAMETERS:
Center Frequency:       5863.5 MHz
Bandwidth (3 dB):       187.4 MHz
Insertion Loss Target:  <= 2.5 dB
Return Loss Target:     >= 11.0 dB
Out-of-Band Rejection:  >= 22.0 dB
Isolation (Duplexer):   >= 22.0 dB
Q Factor:               8230
Temperature Coefficient:-27.7 ppm/°C
Die Size:               1.2 x 1.8 mm
Wafer Size:             8-inch
Number of Resonators:   8
Electrode Material:     Mo
Passivation:            SiO2/Si3N4 stack
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Open Matlab RF Toolbox R2024b and load the Low-Pass Filter template project.
2. Define the substrate stack: Quartz with specified layer thicknesses.
3. Set design targets: center freq 5863.5 MHz, BW 187.4 MHz.
4. Run initial EM simulation with 2D mesh density of 20 cells/wavelength.
5. Optimize resonator geometry using gradient descent (target IL < 2.5 dB).
6. Verify coupling coefficients between resonator stages.
7. Run 3D FEM simulation to account for package parasitics (QFN (Quad Flat No-Lead)).
8. Export GDS-II layout for mask fabrication.
9. Fabricate prototype wafers (8-inch, Quartz).
10. Perform on-wafer probing using Rohde & Schwarz FSW Signal Analyzer.
11. Measure S-parameters (S11, S21, S12, S22) from 100 MHz to 17590 MHz.
12. Compare measured results against simulation and specification limits.
13. Perform temperature cycling (-40°C to +85°C) and re-measure.
14. Document results and generate summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Insertion loss at center frequency shall be <= 2.5 dB
- Return loss in passband shall be >= 11.0 dB
- Out-of-band rejection at +/- 281 MHz offset >= 22.0 dB
- Group delay variation across passband shall be <= 3 ns
- Temperature drift over -40°C to +85°C shall be <= 20.3 MHz
- Power handling shall be >= +28 dBm at 1 dB compression
- ESD tolerance >= 1000 V (HBM)
- Die yield on qualification lot >= 94%
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Measurement Date:       2024-08-14
Devices Tested:         27
Insertion Loss (meas):  2.2 dB
Return Loss (meas):     13.2 dB
Rejection (meas):       25.2 dB
Isolation (meas):       27.1 dB
Q Factor (meas):        8230
Group Delay Variation:  1.6 ns
Power Handling:         +27 dBm
Die Yield:              95.7%

Result Classification:  CONDITIONAL PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Low-Pass Filter design demonstrated acceptable performance for Band 66 (AWS).
b) Insertion loss met target specification.
c) Rejection at near-band offset requires additional resonator tuning.
d) Simulation-to-measurement correlation was within 3% for all key parameters.
e) Wafer-level uniformity was excellent (sigma < 1.5%).
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
1. Review near-band rejection margin for worst-case temperature.
2. Re-run EM simulation with refined mesh for better accuracy.
3. Schedule follow-up measurement after design tweak.
